name: Short Drama

routes._note: NOT A TAB ROOT ANY MORE (docs/design/reference-ui-spec.md §8): the five-tab bar is Home · Explore · My List · Rewards · My Page, and VIP lives in the crown button, the unlock pills and the Membership page. /vip stays a route — the crown's destination until /membership carries every plan (Components/parts/Theme.dsx membershipPath) — and it is PUSHED like every other non-tab page, so no `motion` key here either.

A TAB ROOT now (docs/design/reference-ui-spec.md 8: the fourth tab). `motion: {mobile: none}` is the tab-root declaration — a tab switch is a reset, not a push, so the screen swaps in place and the tab bar never rides a transition (PLAN.md 6.29). Every door that used to PUSH /rewards resets to it now, for the same reason.

_packages_note: THE IN-APP-PURCHASE LANE IS STILL MISSING FROM THIS LIST, AND AS OF 2026-09-02 THE REASON HAS CHANGED. App Store 3.1.1 names in-game currencies and premium-content unlocks as in-app-purchase products, so coins and the VIP pass may not be sold through Stripe inside an iOS or Android build; Stripe is legal on the WEB storefront only. The module that would fix it is Core/Store (scheme 'store', shelf premium like Stripe) at ClosedSource/DSX/Modules/Core/Store. UNTIL 2026-09-02 adding it ABORTED THE BUILD: 'PaywallVIP.dsx:18: <shared.VipCard>: no global component VipCard'. That was a LINTER defect, not the module's - the lint pool folded only configured packages while the build folds every mandatory one, and Foundation's VipCard IS the shared global (PLAN.md 6.115, fixed upstream dev@77f4e65d). Re-measured after the fix with this path and 'store' added: lint 48 files 0 errors, despia build writes the artifact, and BOTH native exports build. WHY IT IS STILL NOT HERE: both native exports read the project's Modules/ folder and the lockfile, never this `packages` list (which is the WEB build's) - so a package declared here by path reaches no device build, has('store') stays false on every native lane, and the purchase surfaces (Components/Store.dsx, Components/parts/PlansSheet.dsx) keep refusing rather than opening a card sheet. The same is true today of Stripe, SocialShare, PostHog and Consent. The ask is filed in PLAN.md 6.115 (one declaration, three lanes). The backend half is complete and asserted by `npm run verify`: POST /store/native, POST /store/restore/native, the RevenueCat <webhook> and its drain. The day the native exports honour this list, add the path below and 'store' to modules, supply the product ids and the RevenueCat secret, and switch payLane to 'iap' where the two comments in Store.dsx and PlansSheet.dsx say so.
_modules_note: DECLARE-THEN-REACH. `modules` is the LINTER's allowlist of platform module schemes this app reaches and no configured `package` claims. `posthog` and `consent` are for Components/parts/Analytics.dsx: Core/PostHog is the framework's product-analytics verb and Core/Consent its gate. They used to be deliberately ABSENT from `packages`, because both shipped a complete web/index.js that no build could load — a browser chunk was emitted only for a manifest that restated `web.entry`, ten modules did, and 98 did not. That was PLAN.md §6.92 and it is fixed upstream: file presence is the gate now (`webLaneEntry`), so declaring them here emits real chunks and has('posthog') can finally answer true. The guards stay on every call regardless — a build that excludes them must still run.

_remind_note: REMIND ME (docs/design/reference-ui-spec.md §2–§2b) is two modules. Core/Notify (scheme `notify`) owns the PERMISSION: `dsx.module.notify.permission()` is the one ladder on three renderers (the kernel's NotifyCore, corpus-pinned), and it is what the permission sheet's 'Allow notifications' asks. Core/LocalPush (scheme `localpush`) owns the SCHEDULE: `send({ seconds, id, title, message, url })` is a one-shot the OS fires at the premiere, after force-quit and reboot, on iOS and Android. The web facet of `send` is a page-side timer that dies with the tab — honest for a delay of minutes, a lie for a premiere in nine days — so Components/App.dsx does not arm it there and says so in the sheet; the server row (server/reminders.dsx) is what survives on every lane. Both packages reach the web build from this list; the native exports read `Modules/` and the lockfile (PLAN.md 6.115), so on a device `has('localpush')` is false until that fold lands and the sheet names the gap instead of pretending.
